turns.q: What do you do outside of work?
turns.answer:
A good chunk of my life goes into street photography — I wander cities with a Leica rangefinder trying to catch those small human moments that mostly don't happen, but occasionally do.[[street-photo]] I also collect photography books, I used to DJ, and I love to cook with music on.[[music]]

Living in Bordeaux with my family keeps me busy too, and I travel whenever I can — I've a soft spot for places with a bad reputation.[[bordeaux]]

turns.q: What do you do outside of work?
turns.answer:
A fair bit, honestly. I'm out on the streets with a Leica most weekends doing street photography[[street-photo]] — it's the hardest kind to do well, and I'm hooked on that. I collect photography books, I've done a lot of travelling (I once spent a year working my way around South East Asia and India), and there's usually music on wherever I am — I used to DJ, so it never really left me.

I live in Bordeaux[[bordeaux]] these days, so cooking and pottering about with family fills a good chunk of the rest.

turns.answer:
A fair few things, but photography's the big one — I shoot street, which is the hardest kind there is: you head out hoping a miracle happens and mostly it doesn't. I also collect photography books, cook a lot, and I'm forever listening to music while I do either. And I love to travel, especially to places with a bit of a bad reputation.

turns.q: What do you do outside of work?
turns.answer:
Photography's the big one — I shoot street, which means walking a city for hours hoping a good frame turns up, and mostly it doesn't. I collect photography books too, and I love cooking with music on in the background[[music]]. And I travel — I'm drawn to places with a bit of a reputation, which is how I've ended up somewhere like Naples or Medellín rather than the postcard spots.
